questions.prompt: In a circular orbit, is gravity absent, balanced away, or providing the inward acceleration?
questions.answer: Gravity is providing the inward acceleration. The satellite is not force-free; its velocity is continually being turned toward the central body.

questions.prompt: Find the circular-orbit speed at radius \(7.5\times10^6\,\mathrm{m}\) around a planet of mass \(6.0\times10^{24}\,\mathrm{kg}\). Use \(G=6.67\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{N\,m^2\,kg^{-2}}\).
Why does the satellite mass not appear in \(v=\sqrt{GM/r}\) for a circular orbit?
questions.answer:
In the circular-orbit balance,
\[
G\frac{Mm}{r^2}=m\frac{v^2}{r}
\]
the satellite mass \(m\) appears on both sides and cancels. The required orbital speed is set by the central mass and orbital radius, not by the satellite mass.

questions.prompt: A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius \(7.5\times10^6\,\mathrm{m}\) with speed \(7.3\times10^3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Estimate its period.
A satellite has circular-orbit period \(5400\,\mathrm{s}\) around a planet of mass \(5.0\times10^{24}\,\mathrm{kg}\). Find the orbital radius.
A circular orbit has radius \(8.0\times10^6\,\mathrm{m}\) and period \(7000\,\mathrm{s}\). Find the local gravitational field magnitude from the orbit data.
One circular orbit has radius \(r\). Another around the same body has radius \(4r\). Compare their speeds and periods.
questions.answer:
Circular-orbit speed scales as
\[
v\propto r^{-1/2}
\]
so at \(4r\),
\[
v_{4r}=\frac{v_r}{2}
\]
The period scales as
\[
T\propto r^{3/2}
\]
so
\[
T_{4r}=4^{3/2}T_r=8T_r
\]
